subject: sociology
chapter_title: Change and Development in Industrial Society

concepts.title: Alienation and the Detailed Division of Labour
concepts.definition: A factory breaks production into many narrow steps, so each worker completes only a fragment and never sees the finished good. Marx named the resulting condition alienation: the worker neither enjoys the task nor controls it, treats the job purely as a way of staying alive, and can be dropped altogether once machines leave no room for human effort.
concepts.key_idea: The classic sociologists tied industry to city living, anonymous workplace ties replacing village familiarity, and repetitive exhausting tasks; marx stressed that piecework without a visible product turns employment into bare survival.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.1 (marx, weber, durkheim on industry; alienation passage)
question_patterns: what did marx mean by the alienation of a mill weaver in industrial work

solution_steps.explain: fragmented tasks, no sight of the end product, no enjoyment of the work, employment hanging on whether technology still has room for human labour

solution_steps.action: check the classic trio's picture of industrial society
solution_steps.explain: marx, weber and durkheim linked industry with urbanisation and anonymous professional relationships replacing the face-to-face ties of rural life

concepts.title: Sectoral Shares of Employment in India
concepts.definition: India spreads its workers very unevenly across the economy. In 2018-19 the primary sector - farming at 42.5 percent plus mining at 0.4 percent - still held the biggest block of workers even though farming's slice of income has fallen sharply and services now produce more than half of growth, a mismatch that strands most earners in low-income occupations.
concepts.key_idea: With roughly 43 percent of workers in primary activity and only about a third in services, the sector employing the most people adds comparatively little to what they earn.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.2 (2018-19 sector shares: agriculture 42.5, mining 0.4, manufacturing 12.1, trade 12.6, transport 5.9, community services 13.8)
question_patterns: in 2018-19 about 42.5 percent of indian workers were in agriculture and 0.4 percent in mining - find the share of employment outside the primary sector

why is it a serious problem that the sector employing the most indians generates comparatively little income

solution_steps.explain: farming 42.5 percent plus mining 0.4 percent gives the primary block
everything outside farming and mining is the non-farm share of employment

worked_examples.q: What share of Indian workers did farming hold in 2018-19: 42.5 percent or 4.25?

concepts.title: Employment Status: Self-employed, Regular and Casual Workers
concepts.definition: Only about a quarter of indian workers hold regular salaried posts; over half are self-employed, ranging from plumbers and street vendors to tutors and freelance photographers, and roughly a quarter toil as casual wage earners. This split explains why secure, benefit-backed jobs remain a minority experience even in a growing economy.
concepts.key_idea: Regular salaried work covers barely 24 percent and casual labour another 24 percent, so more than half of india lives on self-employment without assured wages or benefits.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.2 (employment status chart 1972-73 to 2018-19: 52 percent self-employed, 24 percent regular, 24 percent casual)
question_patterns: over 52 percent of indian workers are self-employed - out of 6 lakh workers, how many would be self-employed

solution_steps.action: convert the percentage share into a fraction
solution_steps.explain: dividing 52 by 100 turns the self-employment share into a multiplier

solution_steps.action: apply the fraction to the workforce
solution_steps.explain: multiplying the total workforce by the fraction yields the self-employed headcount

worked_examples.q: About what share of Indian workers are self-employed: over half or a tenth?

concepts.title: Organised and Unorganised Sectors
concepts.definition: The organised sector covers registered units employing ten or more people through the year, which entitles staff to proper wages, pension and benefits. In india over nine-tenths of all work - on the farm, in the factory or the office - sits outside this protection in the informal sector, where hiring, raises and dismissal run on personal goodwill rather than written rules.
concepts.key_idea: Because registration is rare, union membership thin and workplaces small, secure employment reaches very few indians - of those who do hold it, two-thirds work for the government.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.2 (organised sector definition, over 90 percent informal, two-thirds of secure jobs in government)

solution_steps.explain: informal work of 90 percent leaves at most 10 percent formal

solution_steps.explain: multiplying the workforce by the formal share gives the largest possible organised-sector headcount

concepts.title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Disinvestment
concepts.definition: From the 1990s the government threw open areas once reserved for itself - telecom, civil aviation, power - scrapped industrial licensing, and began selling its stake in public companies, a sale known as disinvestment. Foreign and domestic giants bought up indian firms while others grew multinational, and permanent posts shrank as companies pushed work out to smaller firms, contractors and homes.
concepts.key_idea: Workers read the new policy as a threat: at modern foods, the first company privatised, three-fifths of the staff were pushed to retire within five years, and coca cola's advertising budget of 400 crore dwarfed parle's turnover of 250 crore.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.2 (liberalisation since the 1990s; parle-coca cola; modern foods; disinvestment)
question_patterns: what does disinvestment mean and why do government employees fear it

solution_steps.explain: telecom, civil aviation and power opened to private and foreign investment, industrial licences were abolished, and foreign goods entered indian shops freely
disinvestment is the government selling its share in public sector companies; modern foods was privatised first and 60 percent of its workers retired within five years
companies cut permanent staff and contract work out to smaller firms or homes; small suppliers competing for orders keep wages low and unions find them hard to organise

worked_examples.q: The government selling its stake in public companies is called what?

concepts.title: Jobbers, Contractors and Badli Workers: How Indians Find Work
concepts.definition: Only a small minority lands jobs through advertisements or the employment exchange; personal contacts carry almost everyone. In kanpur's mills the mistri - a jobber drawn from the workers' own region and community - recruited and bossed hands with the owner's backing; today contractors advance loans to village labour for construction sites, and badli hands substitute for permanent workers on leave without gaining their status or security.
concepts.key_idea: Debt still binds labour, but the cash advance owed to a contractor no longer carries the social obligations that tied a farm servant to a landlord, so an industrial worker can break off and seek another employer.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.3 (mistris of kanpur; badli workers; contractor advances; mudra, aatmanirbhar bharat, make in india)
question_patterns: who were the mistris of kanpur's textile mills and what power did they hold over fellow workers

solution_steps.explain: mistris came from the same regions and communities as the workers, held the owner's backing to boss over them, and also put community-related pressures on them; their importance has since declined

the contractor visits villages, lends money including transport cost, treats the loan as an advance wage, and the worker toils unpaid until the debt clears - yet can still break the contract for another employer

solution_steps.action: check badli work and the new schemes
solution_steps.explain: badli workers stand in for permanent staff on leave, some for years without the same security, while mudra, aatmanirbhar bharat and make in india aim at employment and self-employment for sc, st and backward classes

worked_examples.q: In Kanpur's mills, the jobber drawn from the workers' own region was called the what: mistri or munim?

concepts.title: Machine-Paced Work and Rest-Time Arithmetic
concepts.definition: Management has two levers for squeezing out more output: stretch the working day or raise production within each hour. On a car assembly line the machine sets the tempo, so rest is rationed to the minute - adding the short tea pauses and the lunch break shows how little of the shift actually belongs to the worker.
concepts.key_idea: At maruti udyog two cars leave the line every minute while workers get only forty-five minutes of rest in a whole day, and just-in-time delivery of parts every two hours keeps the pace tense; most are worn out by age forty.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.4 (maruti udyog: two cars per minute, two 7.5 minute tea breaks, half hour lunch, just-in-time parts)
question_patterns: at maruti udyog workers get two tea breaks of 7.5 minutes each and a half hour lunch - what percent of an eight hour shift is rest

solution_steps.explain: two breaks of 7.5 minutes each come to 15 minutes of tea time
the tea total plus the half hour lunch gives all the rest time in the day

solution_steps.action: express rest as a percentage of the shift
solution_steps.explain: dividing rest time by the shift length and scaling by 100 gives the rest share

concepts.title: Working Conditions, Mines Law and Migrant Hands
concepts.definition: Statutes such as the mines act of 1952, since folded into the 2020 occupational safety code, cap weekly hours, require overtime pay and lay down safety rules - yet small mines and quarries dodge them through sub-contractors who skip proper worker registers, dodging responsibility for accidents and benefits. Underground miners face floods, fires, roof falls and gas leaks, and many develop silicosis or tuberculosis.
concepts.key_idea: Migrant crews staff the hardest jobs far from home - coal mining alone engages 5.5 lakh workers, and coastal fish processing plants house ten to twelve single young women from the southern states in one small room.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.5 (mines act 1952, occupational safety health and working condition code 2020, coal 5.5 lakh workers, fish processing migrants)
question_patterns: which 1952 law governed hours and safety in mines, and which 2020 code absorbed it

what does the chapter say about the rate of accidents in india's mines compared with other countries

solution_steps.explain: the mines act 1952 - now inside the occupational safety, health and working condition code 2020 - fixes maximum weekly hours, overtime pay and safety rules, followed mainly in big companies

underground dangers include flooding, fire, collapse of roofs and sides, gas emissions and ventilation failures; overground workers brave sun, rain, blasting and falling objects, and breathing diseases like tuberculosis and silicosis are common

fish processing plants on the coast employ mostly single young women from tamil nadu, karnataka and kerala, ten to twelve to a small room, while men migrate singly - trading joint family life for loneliness, though young women gain some economic autonomy

worked_examples.q: Which act of 1952 laid down safety rules for mines: the Mines Act or the Factories Act?

concepts.title: Home-Based Work and the Bidi Chain
concepts.definition: Lace, zari, brocade, carpets, agarbattis and bidis are largely made inside homes, chiefly by women and children paid by the piece. An agent delivers raw material and collects the finished lots; in the bidi trade a villager plucking tendu leaves in forest areas can gather about a hundred bundles a day, each holding fifty leaves, before auctions pass the leaves down through contractors to home rollers and on to pan shops.
concepts.key_idea: Piece rates hide a long chain of middlemen - leaves move from collector to forest department to auction to contractor to home worker, and every hand in the sequence keeps the pay thin.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.6 (bidi industry: 100 bundles a day, 50 leaves each, agent and piece-rate system)
question_patterns: a bidi leaf collector gathers 100 bundles a day with 50 leaves per bundle - how many leaves does the collector handle daily

solution_steps.explain: each tendu bundle holds fifty leaves

solution_steps.action: multiply the day's bundles by the bundle size
solution_steps.explain: a collector averages one hundred bundles a day, so the daily leaf count is bundles times leaves per bundle

concepts.title: Strikes, Lockouts and the 1982 Bombay Textile Strike
concepts.definition: When bargaining fails, workers stop work together in a strike, while a lockout is the employer's counter of shutting the gate against them. Calling a strike is risky: managers can try substitute labour and families run short without wages. The 1982 bombay textile strike under datta samant held out nearly two years and drew about a quarter of a million workers, yet roughly one lakh never returned to the mills.
concepts.key_idea: The failed strike remade mumbai - displaced millhands drifted to villages, casual work or powerloom towns like bhiwandi and malegaon, while owners left machinery to rust and now sell mill land to real estate builders.
concepts.textbook_ref: lesy205.txt, section 5.7 (strike vs lockout; bombay textile strike 1982, datta samant, quarter of a million workers, one lakh jobs lost)

solution_steps.action: scale the job losses against the strikers
solution_steps.explain: divide the jobs lost by the total number of strikers

solution_steps.action: convert the fraction to a percentage
solution_steps.explain: multiplying by 100 expresses the job-loss share in percent
